On an asymptotic fundamental ray, the hypothesis that \(Q\) and \(R\) share no fundamental ray yields \(|\Re R(z)|\ge c|z|^k\) with fixed sign. Positive sign makes \(|AB|=\exp(\Re R)\) exponentially large; bounded \(F\) would force the ratio \(A/B=\exp(2Q-R)\to-1\), contradicting Lemma 3.4 with \(Q_1=2Q\), \(Q_2=R\). Negative sign makes \(|AB|\) exponentially small; bounded \(F\) and polynomial growth of \(P\) force exactly one exponential to dominate on each outer connected branch, while the other tends to zero, contradicting Theorem 1.1 for either \(\exp(Q)+P\) or \(\exp(\widetilde Q)+P\). The source hypotheses are satisfied because \(\deg R<\deg Q\), \(2Q\) has the same fundamental rays as \(Q\), and both \(Q\) and \(\widetilde Q\) are nonconstant.
